title: Service areas and their assigned workers
moduleTitle: App: Field service operations (proposed module; not in curriculum/structure yet)
audience: Owners and office staff who schedule, dispatch and record field jobs. No developer knowledge is needed.
learningOutcomes: Define a service area with a clear boundary and a parent area where one exists.
Place a worker in an area as main base, backup area, or temporary cover.
Explain why an oversized area slows scheduling and dispatch.

instruction.heading: What a service area is
instruction.body: A service area is a region your team covers. It might follow suburbs, council zones, a postcode group, or a travel radius from your yard. Areas help the app decide which workers are sensible for a job. A worker based on the north side should not be sent across the city without a reason. When you build a hierarchy, create the widest area first and then the smaller areas beneath it. Each area needs an address or map point so the app can work out travel time.

instruction.heading: Sizing and membership roles
instruction.body: Oversized areas make scheduling slow and dispatch hard to manage. The reference guide suggests keeping an area to about fifty workers, about a thousand visits a day, and no more than twenty qualified workers for a single visit. Treat these as starting points to review, not as Australian standards. Membership records say which area a worker belongs to. A primary area is where the worker mostly works, usually near home. A secondary area is somewhere they can be sent when needed. A relocation area is a temporary home area for a set period. Each worker's home base needs a confirmed map point, or the app cannot calculate their travel.

procedure: List your service regions and describe the boundary of each.
Create the widest area first, then the smaller areas inside it.
Record a map point for each area and for each worker's home base.
Add each worker as a member, marking their main, backup or temporary role, and dates where needed.
Check that no area holds more workers or visits than the sizing guidance suggests.

workedExamples.situation: Your team covers the inner west and the eastern suburbs. A gardener lives in the east but has been asked to cover the west for six weeks.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What membership role and dates do you record for the gardener?
workedExamples.reasoning: A temporary move calls for a relocation role with a from date and a to date. During those dates the west acts as the gardener's home area for scheduling. The east stays as their primary area afterwards.

equipmentAndPpe: A device with the Titan Zero Field app, where the lesson uses it

commonErrors.error: Drawing one large area for the whole city.
commonErrors.prevention: Split areas by realistic travel range and check the per-area counts.

commonErrors.error: Saving a worker without a confirmed home base point.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the address resolves to a map point before saving the membership.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers app records and office process only. It does not grant, confirm or replace any licence, certificate or authority, and it makes no legal claim.

qualityStandard: Every area has a boundary description and a map point.
Every worker has exactly one primary area.
documentationEvidence: Area list with boundaries and parent areas
Membership roles with from and to dates
summary: Areas tell the app where work happens and who can reasonably attend.
Primary, secondary and relocation roles affect which visits a worker is offered.
Oversized areas slow scheduling, so keep each area to a size you can manage.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which membership role fits a worker who is moving to a new area for three months?
What is the main problem with a very large service area?
options: Workers cannot log in to the app at all on site
Scheduling and dispatch become slow and hard to manage
Customers cannot see the area on the website

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does each worker's home base need a confirmed map point?
options: So the app can calculate travel from it
So the worker's phone number can be verified
So the worker's pay rate can be set
